title: Limits of the level-independent fall: level superpositions, records, the operator under the factor

key_results.statement: Exact in the gradients and in $\kappa$, for every body of $\mathcal C_{\rm lev}$ with linear level profiles, every start $\Phi_\sigma[\alpha,g]$, every $\chi$, $\lambda$ and chain: $p_x=\sum_k\lvert\alpha_k\rvert^2p^{(k)}_x$ and $\bar x_{\rm lab}=\sum_k\lvert\alpha_k\rvert^2\bar x_k$; it rests on the conservation of the level and the orthonormality of the $\lvert f_k\rangle$.

For every start $\Phi_\sigma[\alpha,g]$ concentrated at $p_0$, at first order in the gradients (fixed $\lambda$, start, chain; long chain; window $\Lambda\to\infty$; then $\delta p\to0$) and leading order in $\kappa$: the drift acceleration is $\sum_k\lvert\alpha_k\rvert^2a_{k,\sigma}(p_0)$, with an exact $1/\Lambda$ bound for every window; it is the same for all $\alpha$ iff $a_{k,\sigma}(p_0)$ is level-independent, which at rest is line 1 or 2 of (4.19) with no new condition.

For starts $\Phi_\sigma[\alpha,g]$ at rest, first order in the gradients, long chain, fixed smooth $g$: $D(\lambda)=\tfrac14\lambda^4\operatorname{Var}_\alpha(\langle a_{\cdot,\sigma}\rangle_g)+E$ with $\lvert E\rvert\le r\lambda^3\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}_\alpha}+r^2\lambda^2$ for all $\lambda\ge0$; the $\lambda^4$ part dominates for $\lambda\gg r/\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}_\alpha}$, and its coefficient tends to $\tfrac14\operatorname{Var}_\alpha(a_{\cdot,\sigma}(0))$ for $\delta p\to0$, taken last.

Class $\mathcal C$ with $\lvert\alpha_k\rvert^2=1/N$, starts at rest, sharp-label limit of the $\lambda^4$ part of $D$: $0$ for the variants (a), (c); $\tfrac14\lambda^4\tau^4g^2m^2\mathcal V_N$ for (b1), (b2); $\tfrac14\lambda^4\tau^4g^2c_{\rm f}^2\mathcal V_N$ for (f), in both branches.

At zero gradients, exactly, the level component $k$ of $\Phi_\sigma[\alpha,g]$ has the constant velocity $\sigma\langle\omega_k'\rangle_g\to\sigma\omega_k'(p_0)$ for $\delta p\to0$; in the class $\mathcal C$ no two levels have equal velocities for $\sin2p_0\neq0$; in $\mathcal C_{\rm lev}$ two levels with different data have equal velocities at one such $p_0$ under one condition that needs $\tau_k\neq\tau_{k'}$, and at all $p_0$ iff $(\tau_k,M_k)=(\tau_{k'},M_{k'})$.
Exact in the gradients, infinite chain, any normalized level component: $\mathrm d\bar p_k/\mathrm d\lambda=-\int\frac{\mathrm dp}{2\pi}c^\dagger B_kc+(c^\dagger B_kc)(p_0+\pi)$.

For branch starts at rest, first order in the gradients at fixed $\lambda$ and start, long chain, then $\delta p\to0$ (no window needed): the mean label of the level $k$ changes at the rate $\mathcal F_k-\sigma G_k$; the rate is level-independent iff $\mathcal F_k-\sigma G_k$ is, and together with a level-independent drift acceleration $a\neq0$ iff in addition $\tau_k^2/M_k$ is level-independent, which is impossible in the class $\mathcal C$.

Clock-label reading of $\Phi_\sigma[\alpha,g]$: $P(a;\lambda)=\frac1N\sum_{k,k'}\alpha_{k'}^{*}\alpha_k\Gamma_{kk'}(\lambda)e^{2\pi i(k-k')a/N}$, exact when the level components include the medium; at leading order in $\kappa$ ($\kappa\to0$ at fixed $\lambda$, chain and start) $\Gamma_{kk'}$ is that of the effective body contract.

For every smooth $g$, exactly at zero gradients: $\Gamma^{(0)}_{kk'}=e^{-i(V_k-V_{k'})\lambda}\langle\cos\tfrac{\theta_k-\theta_{k'}}2e^{-i\sigma(\omega_k-\omega_{k'})\lambda}\rangle_g$; for even $g$ only, $\Gamma_{kk'}$ is exactly even in the gradients, so $\lvert\Gamma_{kk'}\rvert$ has no first-order term.

Order estimate, not a bound, for real Gaussian even starts at rest (E1) with $\delta p\ll\min(1,M_k/\tau_k)$, in the range (E3) $\lvert\pi_k\rvert\lambda\ll M_k/\tau_k$, $\lvert\nu_k-\nu_{k'}\rvert\lambda\,\delta p^2\ll1$ and $\lambda\gg\tau_k/M_k^2$, at second order in the gradients at fixed $\lambda$ and start and leading order in $\kappa$: $1-\lvert\Gamma_{kk'}\rvert/\lvert\Gamma^{(0)}_{kk'}\rvert\simeq\tfrac12\delta x^2(\pi_k-\pi_{k'})^2\lambda^2+\tfrac{\lambda^4}{32\delta x^2}\varpi_{kk'}^2$ with $\pi_k=\mathcal F_k-\sigma G_k$; for a level-independent fall $a$ it vanishes iff $a=0$ or $\tau_k^2/M_k=\tau_{k'}^2/M_{k'}$.

Exact, for every smooth $g$, every $p_0$ and $\lambda$, both branches and every body of $\mathcal C_{\rm lev}$ with linear level profiles (effective body contract): $\Gamma_{kk'}[g;\text{gradients}]=\Gamma_{kk'}[g^-;-\text{gradients}]$ with $g^-(p)=g(-p)$; hence the first deviation of $\lvert\Gamma_{kk'}\rvert$ is of second order for every start of definite parity $g^-=\pm g$, and for every start if $(\tau_k,M_k)=(\tau_{k'},M_{k'})$.

First-order term of $\Gamma_{kk'}$ in the gradients for every smooth complex $g$ (fixed $\lambda$ and start, infinite chain, leading order in $\kappa$): an explicit label integral that is exact inside the branch $\sigma$, plus an inter-branch part $\Gamma^{(1),\perp}_{kk'}$ that is only estimated; the first-order term of $\lvert\Gamma_{kk'}\rvert/\lvert\Gamma^{(0)}_{kk'}\rvert$ is $\operatorname{Re}(\Gamma^{(1)}_{kk'}/\Gamma^{(0)}_{kk'})$.

For every body of $\mathcal C_{\rm lev}$ with linear level profiles, every branch start $B_{k,\sigma}[g]$ and every $\chi$, at first order jointly in $G_k$, $\mathcal F_k$, $g_{\zeta,k}$ and $\kappa(\xi-\langle X\rangle)$ at fixed $\lambda$, start and chain: the first-order velocity does not change when $X$ is not sharp in $\chi$, so (4.7), (4.16), (4.19) are unchanged.

Zero gradients of the effective body contract, fixed label $p$ and fixed $\varepsilon=\kappa(\xi-\langle X\rangle)$, all $\lambda\ge0$: the coefficient $v_2(p,\lambda)$ of $\varepsilon^2$ in the velocity of a branch start, in closed form, with the secular part $\tfrac12\sigma\lambda^2\omega'''$.

Zero gradients of the effective body contract, every branch start with smooth $g$ and every $\chi$ with finite moments of $X$; Taylor expansion in $\kappa$ at fixed $\lambda$, start and chain: $v=\sigma\langle\omega_k'\rangle_g+\kappa^2\sigma_X^2[\tfrac12\lambda^2\sigma\langle\omega_k'''\rangle_g+R_2]+\kappa^3\mu_3[-\tfrac16\lambda^3\sigma\langle\omega_k''''\rangle_g+R_3]+O(\kappa^4)$; $R_2$ has an exact bound linear in $\lambda$ at fixed $g$ (not uniform for $\delta p\to0$), $R_3=O(\lambda^{5/2})$ is an order estimate.

Zero gradients, sharp label $p_0$ (expansion in $\kappa$ at fixed $\lambda$; window average; then $\delta p\to0$): $\delta a^{(2)}_{k,\sigma}=-\kappa^2\sigma_X^2\lambda\,v\,(4+3\omega_k''/\omega_k)$, zero at rest, of first order in $v$, the same in both branches at given $v$; level-independent at leading order in $v$ iff $\tau_k/M_k$ is, which fails in the class $\mathcal C$.

Same class and limits as (7.15): $\delta a^{(3)}_{k,\sigma}=-\tfrac12\kappa^3\mu_3\lambda^2\sigma\omega_k''''(p_0)$, at rest $\tfrac\sigma2\kappa^3\mu_3\lambda^2\tfrac{\tau_k^2}{M_k}(4+\tfrac{3\tau_k^2}{M_k^2})$: odd in the branch, present only for a skewed distribution of $X$, level-dependent in the class $\mathcal C$.

The record terms of (7.15) at leading order in $v$ and of (7.16) at rest, in the background of (17.15) of 03-ilang-space/17-motion with $d_0=\kappa\sigma_X$, $v_{\max,k}=\tau_kd_0$, $u=d_0v$ and $\gamma_X=\mu_3/\sigma_X^3$: the change of $\mathrm d^2\bar x/\mathrm d\lambda^2$ is $[-\lambda(4d_0^2+3v_{\max,k}^2/M_k^2)u+\tfrac{\sigma\gamma_X}2\lambda^2\tfrac{v_{\max,k}^2}{M_k}(4d_0^2+3v_{\max,k}^2/M_k^2)]\hat e$.

The record terms are smaller than the drift acceleration (4.7) at rest where $\varrho_2<1$ and $\varrho_3<1$, that is $\lambda<\lambda_2\propto\lvert\sigma\mathcal F_k-G_k\rvert/(\kappa^2\lvert v\rvert)$ and $\lambda<\lambda_3\propto(\lvert\sigma\mathcal F_k-G_k\rvert/\kappa^3)^{1/2}$; a fall that is level-independent to the relative accuracy $\delta_{\rm acc}$ needs $\varrho_2,\varrho_3\le\delta_{\rm acc}$ for every level on the whole observed range of $\lambda$ and $v$.

On-site block $(1+gx)[M_k\sigma_3+u_k\mathbb 1_2]-\mathcal F_Ux\,\mathbb 1_2$, any $\tau_k$ and $g_{\zeta,k}$, branch starts at rest, drift acceleration at first order in the gradients (long window, sharp label) and leading order in $\kappa$: $a_{k,\pm}(0)=-g\tau_k^2\pm\tfrac{\tau_k^2}{M_k}(\mathcal F_U-gu_k)$.

Same class as (7.19): the fall from rest is level-independent in the upper branch iff $\tau_k^2[(\mathcal F_U-gu_k)/M_k-g]$ is, in the lower branch iff $\tau_k^2[-(\mathcal F_U-gu_k)/M_k-g]$ is, and in both with one value $a$ iff $gu_k=\mathcal F_U$ and $g\tau_k^2=-a$ for all $k$; for $\tau_k=\tau$ the first two coincide for every $g$.

Under $C_{\rm eff}\mapsto C_{\rm eff}+c\,\mathbb 1$ the parameters change as $(u_k,\mathcal F_U)\mapsto(u_k+c,\mathcal F_U+gc)$; well defined are $g$, $M_k$, $u_k-u_{k'}$ and $\mathcal F_U-gu_k$; not well defined are $u_k$, the statement $u_k=0$ for all $k$ and the statement $u_k\propto M_k$.

Table of the orders in the gradients, $v$, $M_k/\tau_k$, $\kappa$ and $\lambda$ at which the lattice, the drift velocity, a superposition of levels, the records, the operator under the factor and a plain gradient change the level-independent fall and the relation (4.24); the row on the superposition of levels states the order of $\lvert\Gamma_{kk'}\rvert$ separately for starts of definite parity (second order) and for starts at rest that are not of definite parity (first order).

open_issues: The coefficients of (7.10) are an order estimate under (E1)–(E3) (Gaussian even start, within-branch transport, equal spreading); a bound, and the second-order term for other starts of definite parity, are not derived.

(7.25) and (7.26) are order estimates under (F1)–(F3): the remainder is estimated, not bounded. For a start at rest that is not of definite parity with ⟨p³⟩_g = J_g = 0, and for a pair of levels with Δν_kk' = 0 and unequal data, the first-order term of |Γ_kk'| is at most of the size of the remainder (F3); whether it vanishes is not determined. Outside (F2), |Δν_kk'| λ δp² ≳ 1, only (7.24) is available. The second-order term of a start that is not of definite parity is not derived.
R_3 = O(λ^(5/2)) in (7.14) and the window suppression O(1/(M_k Λ)) of the oscillating terms for a sharp label are order estimates; only R_2 has an exact bound, and it is not uniform in δp → 0.
The estimate ϱ_2 ≲ λ²(4 d_0² + 3 v_max,k²/M_k²) for a fall from rest mixes κ² with a gradient (third order, out of scope) and is not derived.
(7.17) uses v_max,k = τ_k d_0 for level-dependent τ_k; the quoted bound (5.11) of 04-ilang-time/05-moving-clock is stated for one τ.

The effect of an operator under the factor on the relation (4.24) outside the class C (for example u_k = u_* + w M_k with w ≠ 0) needs the clock rate of that body, which is not among the quoted inputs.
